term: ECS Launch Types: EC2 vs Fargate
definition: EC2 launch type: you provision and manage the container instances. Fargate: serverless, you only define task CPU and memory. Remember: no servers to manage means Fargate.
Scales the number of ECS tasks with target tracking, step, scheduled, or predictive policies, using CPU, memory, or load balancer requests per target. It scales tasks, not EC2 instances.
Private and public container image registry, backed by S3 and secured with IAM. Supports vulnerability scanning, lifecycle policies to expire images, and cross-Region or cross-account replication.

Mount an EFS file system into ECS tasks, including Fargate, for persistent storage shared across tasks and Availability Zones. Data survives task restarts. Classic exam answer for shared container storage.
Both restrict private CloudFront content to authorized users. Signed URL: access to one file. Signed cookies: access to many files without changing URLs. Not the same as S3 presigned URLs.
Synchronous: API Gateway or load balancers, and the caller waits. Asynchronous: SQS, SNS, Kinesis, or EventBridge, and the caller moves on. Asynchronous decouples services and absorbs spikes.
Managed document database compatible with MongoDB. Built like Aurora: storage grows automatically and is replicated across three Availability Zones. Remember: MongoDB on AWS means DocumentDB.
Serverless, managed database compatible with Apache Cassandra, using Cassandra Query Language. Data is replicated across three Availability Zones, with on-demand or provisioned capacity.
Amazon QLDB, the ledger database, reached end of support on July 31, 2025. AWS points ledger workloads to Aurora PostgreSQL. Older practice questions may still show QLDB.

term: EC2 High Availability with Elastic IP
definition: Auto Scaling group with minimum, maximum and desired of one across two Availability Zones. User data plus an instance role reattaches the Elastic IP address to the replacement instance.
Cache at the CloudFront edge, in API Gateway, then ElastiCache or DAX near the database. Caching closer to users is faster but risks staler data; tune time to live values.
Automated account checks for cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence. The full set of checks needs Business Support Plus or higher.
Free console tool: answer questions about a workload for each pillar, get high and medium risks flagged, and track an improvement plan with milestones. Supports extra lenses such as serverless.
Stop guessing capacity, test systems at production scale, automate experiments, allow evolutionary architectures, drive decisions with data, and improve through game days.
